dataset.used: orthophoto, trace annotation and DEM patches of the sites OG1, KB3 and EN; no file of the dataset is redistributed, this record holds statistics only

notes: The patches are not georeferenced: the pixel size is taken at the two ends of the range given in the literature (keys of by_pixel_mm and dark_band_width_mm), and every quantity that uses it is given for both.

Valid pixels: alpha > 0, or not pure white connected to the patch border in three-channel images; elevation finite and above -1000 (no-data value -32767). Annotation pixels outside the valid domain are not sample points: mosaic.annotation_px_outside_valid counts them and mosaic.annotation_px counts those inside.

stitching: median and 90th percentile of the absolute elevation step across the shared edges of adjacent patches, for the two readings of the file names; the patches were assembled with the reading named in "chosen".

Sample points of the occlusion analysis are skeleton pixels, counted without arc-length weights. Rows of by_pixel_mm: one per off-nadir angle beta_deg and clearance height clearance_m; "across" and "along" pool the two sides or directions (side_shares gives each), so their counts are twice the number of sample points.

occluded_share excludes the undetermined points (line of sight left the valid DEM before reaching the clearance height) from the denominator; occluded_share_undetermined_as_visible counts them all as not occluded and is a lower bound; undetermined_share is their share of all sample points.
elevation_grid: OG1 has few runs of identical or linearly interpolated values (DEM on the image grid); in KB3 the DEM changes every 4 image pixels and in EN every 2.

Profiles use the ruler of geocrack_comparison.py (every 8th skeleton pixel, +-63 px, Rec. 709 brightness); points whose profile passes through invalid pixels are dropped. Quantiles are over the measurement points of a site.

synthetic_reference: the same readings along the target layer of the 50 frames of the multi-illumination aerial set. Its histograms are weighted so that every frame has a total weight of 1 over its measurement points; they are what the overlapping coefficients of vs_synthetic are computed with, and its dark_band_width_mm.p5 and p95 bound the shares below, inside and above.

vs_synthetic.width_mm.*.median_position: "narrower" when the median width of the site is below the synthetic 5th percentile, "wider" when it is above the 95th, otherwise "inside". The widths of EN are not compared.

illumination.azimuth_image_deg is in the image frame (degrees from +x towards +y, y down), not a compass bearing; it is taken as the horizontal azimuth of the sun. The regression cannot separate direct light from albedo that varies with aspect. illumination.spearman_phi_brightness_difference is reproducible to within about 0.0001: values of phi that are equal in exact arithmetic can differ in their last bits, and their rank order follows the last bits of the estimated azimuth, which can differ between runs.
The line-of-sight computation of the stored record ran in single precision on a GPU ("device").

elevation_grid.method: 400 rows sampled: runs of identical values (+1) and runs of zero second difference (+2), lengths in image pixels; share = pixels covered by such runs / valid pixels of the sampled rows
